title: Internet of Agents: Weaving a Web of Heterogeneous Agents for Collaborative Intelligence
venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2025), spotlight
summary: Notes that existing multi-agent frameworks struggle to integrate third-party agents built in other ecosystems, are mostly single-device, and rely on hard-coded communication pipelines. IoA proposes an Internet-inspired platform with an agent integration protocol, an instant-messaging-style architecture, and dynamic mechanisms for team formation and conversation-flow control. Experiments on general-assistant, embodied and retrieval-augmented generation tasks show it outperforming prior baselines in coordinating heterogeneous agents.
relevance: Directly tackles collaboration among heterogeneous, distributed agents from different frameworks, the setting where cross-framework delegation and migration must work.

title: Building A Secure Agentic AI Application Leveraging A2A Protocol
summary: Provides a security analysis of Google's Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, situating it in the history of agent communication. Using the MAESTRO threat-modeling framework, it examines risks around Agent Card management, task execution integrity and authentication, recommends secure development practices, and discusses how combining A2A with MCP can support secure interoperability.
relevance: Analyses the security of A2A task delegation, the primary handoff mechanism studied by the corpus.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): Landscape, Security Threats, and Future Research Directions
summary: Studies MCP from architectural and security perspectives by defining an MCP server lifecycle of four phases (creation, deployment, operation, maintenance) and building a threat taxonomy across four attacker types. Real-world case studies illustrate the attack surfaces, and the paper proposes phase-specific safeguards and reviews MCP's industry adoption and tooling.
relevance: Characterises the trust and security risks of the tool-access layer that any moved agent must re-bind to at its destination.
